documentation.rationale: Split result. Identity and terms (a) are weak for a private listing: no VIN, no plate, no title photo, no history report, though price, mileage, colors and equipment are stated and the price history is visible. Maintenance and condition evidence (b) is unusually detailed for Facebook - a mileage-itemised log from 104,971 to 126,462 mi covering six oil changes, a full fluid/plug service at 105k, a timing-cover check at 119k and OEM front brakes at 126k, plus a complete itemised mod list naming the installing shop. But it is the seller's own typed document, not shop invoices, and the first ~105,000 miles and 13 years of the car's life have no record at all.

condition.rationale: Positives are real: recent OEM front pads and rotors, a documented 105k major fluid service including coolant, transmission and plugs, a timing-cover inspection noting no coolant leak, quality named-brand hardware installed by a shop rather than driveway parts. Against that, every model-critical wear item is unverified - KDSS hydraulic condition, secondary air injection, valley plate, transfer case actuator - and the truck carries a Stage 4 lift, winch, steel bumpers and 285s that load bearings, CVs and bushings harder than stock. Photos were not captured here, so cosmetics, underbody and the cut body-mount areas are not examined.

price_value.rationale: $22,500 (down from $25,000 after eight weeks) for a 2010 at 128k. Comparable 2010s trade far lower: a 2010 Premium with 173,709 mi asks $16,995 in Modesto, a 2010 base with 142,900 mi sold at $14,250, a 2010 Premium with 230k sold at $9,800, and a 2012 Luxury at 118k sold for $17,500 in Orange, CA. Even allowing this one is the best-mileage 2010 in the set, the stock-equivalent value is roughly $16-18k; the ask is asking Jason to pay for a $15k build whose resale recovery is typically 20-30 cents on the dollar and which his own brief treats as no-premium or a negative. The irreversible body-mount chop and viper cut narrow the future buyer pool.

mission_fit.rationale: This genuinely supplies what the RX 350 does not: body-on-frame, low range, a custom roof rack, a custom-fit sleeping platform and all-terrain tires - the exact two camping formats in the brief. But the brief also says heavy off-road hardware (big lift, winch, armour) earns no premium and can be a negative because it signals hard use, and this truck is built well past 'quality rack and sensible tires'. Fuel economy (15/20 stock, worse lifted on 285s) makes it a poor bridge commuter, and it overlaps the RX for ordinary family duty.

logistics.rationale: Redwood City is about 75-80 miles from Carmel - an easy same-day inspection and drive home, with Bay Area Toyota/Lexus and 4x4 specialists available for a PPI including a KDSS check. California car, previously smogged; the seller must supply a current smog certificate at sale. Private seller means no doc fees. The only open logistics item is whether the seller will release the VIN and allow an off-site PPI, which has not been tested.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Beige over tan, a well-known and likeable overland platform with real character and a thoughtful build (sleeping platform, roof rack, quality suspension brand). It is nothing like the manual enthusiast brief, but it is not pretending to be; as an adventure-utility object it has appeal. The heavy armour and cut bodywork dull the 'clean, tasteful' preference stated in the capability_intent.

positives: Mileage-itemised ownership log covering 104,971-126,462 mi with a full 105k fluid service (coolant, transmission, differential, brake and power-steering fluid, spark plugs, filters, induction clean), six oil changes, and OEM front pads and rotors at 126,462 mi - far more evidence than a typical Facebook private sale.
Camping capability matches the brief directly: custom-built roof rack plus a custom-fit sleeping platform, i.e. both the in-vehicle sleeping and rooftop-tent formats the buyer actually plans to use.
Owner log records a timing-cover inspection with no coolant leak at 119,000 mi and a smog pass at 121,594 mi - partial, dated answers to two of the 1UR-FE/GX460 expensive-failure questions.
Quality named hardware installed by a shop (ICON, Warn, Total Chaos, Dr KDSS adapters, matching Falken Wildpeak AT3W set with ~20k miles), not improvised parts; powertrain untouched.
75-80 miles from Carmel, California car, private seller, no doc fees - a PPI and a drive home are trivially easy to arrange.

ppi_focus: KDSS: cross-link lean measurement, hydraulic cylinder and line condition, accumulator, and whether the Dr KDSS adapters are correctly shimmed for the Stage 4 lift
Secondary air injection: full OBD-II scan with freeze-frame and readiness monitors, plus a cold-start listen for the pump and valve operation
1UR-FE valley plate and timing cover for coolant seepage and oil weep; verify the 119k 'timing cover checked' claim against what the car actually shows now
Underbody and frame: chopped body mounts and viper cut - weld quality, coating, corrosion; skid plates and crossmembers for impact damage
Front end loaded by lift, steel bumper and winch: ball joints, upper control arm bushings, CV boots and joint angles, wheel bearings, tie rods
Transfer case actuator operation - cycle 4H/4L/neutral - and transfer case fluid condition (no service recorded)
Winch and auxiliary lighting wiring: fusing, battery load test, and whether the harness has been tapped into critical circuits
Roof rack mounting - factory points versus drilled - and headliner/roof rail for water intrusion
Tire date codes, remaining tread across all four and the spare, and evidence of uneven wear from alignment or bearing issues
Extended highway drive at 65-75 mph for driveline vibration, death-wobble tendencies and brake pulsation
what_would_change_verdict: A price at or near stock-equivalent value for a 128k 2010 (roughly $16,500-$18,500, given comps at $14,250-$16,995 with more miles) would turn the build from a cost into a bonus.
A clean specialist PPI with a documented KDSS lean measurement, a full readiness scan with no emissions codes, and clean underbody/cut-area photos would move this up materially.
Shop invoices for the 105k service and the build, plus a VIN and clean history report, would convert the current owner-typed log from claimed to verified.
Evidence of hard trail use, a KDSS leak or lean, P2440/P2442 history without a documented repair, or corrosion at the cut body mounts would move it down sharply.
Seller refusing the VIN or an off-site PPI would end it.
evidence.mission_note: This is a legitimate utility_capability candidate - body-on-frame, low range, roof rack and a fitted sleeping platform deliver camping capability the RX 350 simply does not have - but it is built well beyond the stated intent, and the brief explicitly says heavy off-road hardware (big lift, winch, armour) earns no premium and can signal hard use. In accelerated_bridge mode it is not a bridge car either: poor economy and a heavily modified 16-year-old truck are the opposite of a low-risk daily, so it only makes sense as a deliberate second-purpose vehicle bought at stock-equivalent money.
evidence.rationale: Evidence quality here is better than a typical Facebook private sale but still short of verified. The attached seller document is genuinely useful: a mileage-itemised log from 104,971 to 126,462 miles showing six oil changes, a full fluid and spark plug service at 105k, a timing-cover inspection with no coolant leak at 119k, a smog pass at 121,594 and OEM front brakes at 126,462 - plus a complete build list naming the installing shop. It is still the owner's own typed log rather than invoices, and it covers only the last 23,000 miles; the first 105,000 miles and 13 years have no record at all. The two expensive GX460 questions remain open: KDSS hydraulic condition is unaddressed (the Dr KDSS adapters confirm the system exists and was lift-corrected, nothing more), and secondary air injection rests on a self-reported smog pass from 6,400 miles ago with no scan. The build is the pricing problem: $22,500, already cut from $25,000 after eight weeks, against 2010 comps at $14,250 sold (142,900 mi), $16,995 asking (173,709 mi) and $9,800 sold (230,000 mi), and a 2012 Luxury at 118k that sold for $17,500 in Orange, CA. Roughly $5-7k of the ask is hardware the buyer's brief says is worth no premium, and the body-mount chop and viper cut are irreversible. On the positive side the mission fit is real - the rack and fitted sleeping platform match exactly the camping formats planned - and logistics are excellent at 75-80 miles from Carmel with easy PPI access. Nothing in the listing establishes a specific current fault, so there is no known-repair charge; the risk is concentrated in what a KDSS and underbody inspection would reveal and in overpaying for someone else's build.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN and the Dirt Direct Offroad and 105k-service invoices, and ask to book an off-site PPI at a Bay Area Toyota/Lexus or 4x4 specialist with explicit KDSS lean measurement, a full readiness scan and underbody photos of the chopped body mounts - then negotiate from stock-equivalent comps, not from the $15k mod spend.
